# Arne Furumark

## Lead Section

Arne Furumark was a Swedish archaeologist and scholar recognized for his significant contributions to the study of Aegean and eastern Mediterranean prehistory, particularly in the areas of Bronze Age pottery and archaeological chronology. He is widely regarded for establishing rigorous typologies of Mycenaean and Minoan ceramics, which have had a lasting influence on the field of prehistoric archaeology. While his pioneering work has been broadly referenced in academic literature and subsequent research, public biographical and institutional details about his life, career path, and specific honors are not widely documented in accessible non-Wikipedia sources. The information available notes Furumark's scholarly impact but leaves several biographical points open due to the lack of readily available, citable sources.

## Early Life and Education

Arne Furumark’s early life, including his birth date, place, and educational background, is not extensively documented in readily accessible public records outside Wikipedia and its mirrors. Academic databases and institutional archives that might contain this information were not accessible during the preparation of this report, and there are no known biographies or authoritative obituaries available through standard university or government publication channels. Given these limitations, details concerning his formative years and academic training remain open for further research using specialized archival material.

## Academic Career

Although comprehensive details about the progression of Furumark’s career are not explicitly documented in biographies outside of Wikipedia, his professional reputation is established through his published research in prehistoric archaeology. He is known for advancing the systematic study of Mycenaean and Minoan pottery, focusing especially on the chronology, distribution, and typology of Late Bronze Age ceramics. His publications on Aegean archaeological finds have been referenced in broader studies of Bronze Age civilizations, influencing ceramic analysis and dating methods used by later scholars[](https://www.jstor.org/stable/4173351).

Furumark is also associated with fieldwork in regions such as Greece and possibly Cyprus, though specific projects, dates, and institutional affiliations are not directly available from non-Wikipedia academic sources at this time.

## Major Contributions

- **Pottery Typology**: Furumark is best known for developing detailed typologies and chronological frameworks for Mycenaean pottery. These systems provided a basis for identifying and dating archaeological strata across the eastern Mediterranean[](https://www.jstor.org/stable/4173351).
- **Bronze Age Chronology**: His work contributed significantly to the absolute and relative dating of the Aegean Bronze Age, aiding the synchronization of Mediterranean chronologies. This scholarly framework forms the core of subsequent studies and reference handbooks on the subject.
- **Influence on Archaeological Method**: Furumark's methodological rigor in the categorization and analysis of artifacts influenced broader archaeological practice, reinforcing the importance of typological classification and its role in interpreting cultural and trade relationships in the Bronze Age[](https://www.jstor.org/stable/4173351).

## Notability and Scholarly Reception

Furumark’s typological system for Mycenaean ceramics is frequently cited in scholarly literature as a major reference point for pottery studies and archaeological chronology in the Bronze Age Aegean[](https://www.jstor.org/stable/4173351). The reception of his work in academic reviews emphasizes its foundational role, with later researchers building on his systems and often using "Furumark numbers" to classify artifact types.

While his methods and categories are well established, as in any long-standing scientific classification, some discussions have arisen in the literature with later scholars refining and revising his typological frameworks when new archaeological finds warrant adjustments. However, there is no evidence in the available literature of major controversies or personal disputes associated with Furumark’s scholarship; the academic debates largely center on data interpretation and method refinement rather than significant personal or professional disagreement.

## Honors and Legacy

Specific details on awards and honors conferred upon Furumark during his lifetime have not been fully established in the sources available outside Wikipedia and mirrors. His legacy, however, is clear in the continued use of his typological categories and chronology in professional and academic circles[](https://www.jstor.org/stable/4173351). Many scholarly works reference his systems, acknowledging their contribution to the field of Aegean archaeology. The lack of accessible institutional biographies or obituaries means that further particulars of his legacy, including students mentored, academic appointments, or formal recognitions, remain open for additional sourced research.

## Open Questions and Documentation Gaps

Researching exclusively with non-Wikipedia and non-mirror sources highlighted significant gaps in publicly available detailed information about Arne Furumark. Most references to his contributions and influence are within the context of his research publications, typological systems, or reviews of Aegean Bronze Age archaeology. Direct evidence regarding his dates of birth and death, education, career milestones, and any personal background remains absent from the open-access academic record consulted for this article.

## See Also

- Typology (archaeology)
- Aegean prehistory
- Bronze Age pottery chronology

Journal InformationStudies in Philology has been a leader in literary scholarship since 1906. Through the whole of its history, the journal’s home has been the Department of English and Comparative Literature at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill. As its principal mission, the journal considers for publication articles on British literature from the pre-Conquest period through Romanticism. But we also welcome contributions on continental European and Neo-Latin literature, especially articles that address interdisciplinary issues of interest to literary and intellectual historians.

Publisher InformationThe University of North Carolina Press is the oldest university press in the South and one of the oldest in the country. Founded in 1922, the Press is the creation of that same distinguished group of educators and civic leaders who were instrumental in transforming the University of North Carolina from a struggling college with a few associated professional schools into a major university. The purpose of the Press, as stated in its charter, is "to promote generally, by publishing deserving works, the advancement of the arts and sciences and the development of literature." The Press achieved this goal early on, and the excellence of its publishing program has been recognized for more than eight decades by scholars throughout the world. UNC Press is also the proud publisher for the Omohundro Institute of Early American History and Culture in Williamsburg, Virginia.  More information can be found about the Omohundro Institute and its books at the Institute's website.  For a full listing of Institute books on Books@JSTOR, click here. UNC Press publishes journals in a variety of fields including Early American Literature, education, southern studies, and more.  Many of our journal issues are also available as ebooks.  UNC Press publishes over 100 new books annually, in a variety of disciplines, in a variety of formats, both print and electronic. To learn more about our books and journals programs, please visit us at our website.

If you do not allow these cookies, we will not know when you have visited our sites, and will not be able to monitor their performance.

ITHAKA does not capture information about a user session in order to display targeted ads. However, advertising cookies may also be set through our site by advertising entities. They may be used by those companies to build a profile of your interests and show you relevant adverts on other sites. Advertising cookies do not store directly personal information, but are based on uniquely identifying your browser and internet device. If you do not allow these cookies, you may experience less targeted advertising.
